info.title: diff-reviewer platform API
info.description:
The review platform: the repositories whose pull requests it reviews, and one review job per review. A job moves `pending → queued → running → draft → approved → posted`; `rejected` is a discarded draft, `stale` a draft whose pull request has moved on, and `failed` a run that ended without a review.

Three credentials, none standing in for another. The password (`$DIFF_REVIEWER_PASSWORD`) is accepted only by `POST /api/login`, which sets the session cookie; failed password logins are rate-limited (an immediate `429` with `Retry-After`), and the API token signs in there too, unlimited. Every route under `/api/v1/` needs the session cookie or the API token (`$DIFF_REVIEWER_API_TOKEN_FILE`) as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Every route under `/api/agent/v1/` needs the agent token (`$DIFF_REVIEWER_AGENT_TOKEN_FILE`) as a bearer, and nothing else reaches it; an agent's requests go through kleis, which supplies it.

Every write must be `application/json` (`415` otherwise). Every write to a job under `/api/v1/` names the job's `version` as last read, and is a `409` if the job has changed since. A request the server fails on is a `500` whose reason goes to the server log; a method a route does not answer is a `405`. Collections answer `{"items": [...]}`. Instants are RFC 3339 in UTC; an absent value is `null`.

Each repository has a rubric document — a default rubric and the pull request types its reviews tell apart, each with a rubric and the categories its comments are filed under — written whole and versioned (`/api/v1/repos/{owner}/{name}/rubrics`). Every write of a job's review, by the agent, a person or (once posted) GitHub, is kept as a revision (`/api/v1/jobs/{id}/revisions`).

Calibration (`/api/v1/repos/{owner}/{name}/calibration/…`) compares the agent's reviews with the reviews the repository's `trustedReviewers` wrote on its closed pull requests: an import stores each such review as a sample, a run makes one `calibration` job per sample at the sample's commit, and each job's draft is scored against its sample. A `calibration` job is queued and run like any other, but is never approved, claimed or posted.

post.summary: Exchange the password, or the API token, for a session cookie

200.description: Signed in; sets the session cookie.

post.description:
Password attempts are counted per client address — an IPv6 client per /64 — the socket's peer, or, for a request from the proxy `--trusted-proxy` names, the last address of its `X-Forwarded-For`. After 5 failures from one address within 15 minutes every password attempt from it, right or wrong, is a `429` for a delay that starts at 15 seconds and doubles with each further failure (at most 15 minutes). After 100 failures from all addresses together, every password attempt is a `429` for a while. A refusal is immediate; `Retry-After` says how long. A success clears its address's count.

The API token signs in too, and no limit counts it or refuses it: it is how the operator gets in while password attempts from everywhere are refused.

get.summary: Whether the caller is signed in

200.description: Every repository, by owner and name.

mode.description: `staged` (default): a person approves each review before it is posted. `direct`: posted as soon as the agent submits it.

autoReview.description: Default `false`: only the jobs asked for are reviewed.

trustedReviewers.description: GitHub logins; stored in lower case, once each. Left out, the current ones are kept.

version.description: The version of the settings last read, 0 for a repository not registered yet. Given, the write is a `409` if the settings have changed since; left out, it is not checked.

put.description: Names are stored in lower case, as GitHub compares them. `mode` and `autoReview` are replaced: a write that omits one sets its default. `trustedReviewers` is kept when omitted, so that a client that does not know it cannot wipe it. Every write increments `version`.

delete.description: Its jobs are kept: they are the record of reviews that happened. So are its rubric versions, which those jobs name: registering the repository again picks its rubric up where it was.

200.description: The jobs of the kind asked for.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Which jobs: reviews (the default), calibration jobs, or all.

post.summary: Ask for a review of a pull request

headSha.description: The head commit the review is for: a whole commit id (40 or 64 hex digits; an abbreviation is a `400`), stored in lower case. Queueing checks it is still the pull request's head, and makes the job `stale` if it is not.

put.description: The body is `{"version": n, "review": {...}}`. Allowed while the job is `pending`, `draft`, `approved` or `rejected` (`409` otherwise: the agent may still be writing it, or it is history), and makes it a `draft`: an approval was of the review as it was. Each comment must name a file and lines `1 ≤ start_line ≤ end_line`, and say something. `409` while a post of the job may have reached GitHub (`postStartedAt` is set). Each comment's `category` is checked against the rubric version the job was reviewed against (the current one if none). Comments without an `id` are given one, and the review is appended to the job's revisions as a person's. A `calibration` job's review is the agent's, scored as submitted, and is not edited: `409`.

post.summary: Make a person's decision on a job
post.description: A person's moves only: `draft → approved | rejected | stale`, `approved → draft`, `rejected → draft`, and `failed → pending` to run the review again (which clears `queueEntry` and `error`; the next attempt is queued under a new orchestra `external_id`). Queueing, running, the agent's draft and posting are the platform's own, and no request makes them — posting is asked for with `POST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/post`. Any other move is a `409`, and so is approving a job without a readable review. `409` while a post of the job may have reached GitHub (`postStartedAt` is set). A `calibration` job is never approved: `409`.

post.summary: Post an approved review to GitHub
post.description: Posts the job's review to its pull request — submitted, pinned to `headSha` with every comment on the right-hand side, its body ending in the marker `<!-- diff-reviewer job <id> -->` — and then marks the job `posted`, recording GitHub's id, URL and body of the review in `postedReview`. The event is the review's decision, except on a pull request the operator (`DIFF_REVIEWER_GITHUB_LOGIN`) wrote, where an approval or a request for changes is posted as a comment and `postNote` says so. The job must be `approved` and at the `version` named, its review valid and its comments on the diff (`409` otherwise). Posting is claimed (`postStartedAt`) immediately before the request to GitHub; a claim less than three times that request's timeout old is a `409`, as a post that may still be under way. An older claim is settled first: the pull request's reviews by the operator are searched for the marker, and a review found is recorded rather than posted again. A `4xx` from GitHub clears the claim and leaves the job `approved` with the reason in `error` (a `502` that carries the job). No answer or a `5xx` keeps the claim, even when the review is not found yet, so the next attempt looks again before posting. `503` when the platform has no GitHub token. A `calibration` job is never posted: `409`.

502.description: GitHub refused the review or could not be reached.

get.description: The unified diff of the pull request at the job's head commit, from its merge base with the base commit — what GitHub shows as the pull request's diff. Fetched from GitHub once per base and head and then kept. `409` for a job that names no head commit yet; `502` when GitHub cannot be read; `503` when the platform has no GitHub token. `413` for a diff past `--max-diff-bytes`.

parameters.name: X-Diff-Reviewer-Job
parameters.description: The job the agent's prompt named (`--job`). Without it, the request is about the pull request's only queued or running job, and with two it is a `409`: an older run must not take over a newer review.

get.summary: The review the agent is running
get.description: The job the agent runs (see `X-Diff-Reviewer-Job`), `queued` or `running`; reading a `queued` one moves it to `running`. `404` when no review of the pull request is being run. `409` too when the repository's rubric cannot be read by this build.

200.description: The job, as the agent needs it.

parameters.name: X-Diff-Reviewer-Job
parameters.description: The job the agent's prompt named (`--job`). Without it, the request is about the pull request's only queued or running job, and with two it is a `409`: an older run must not take over a newer review.

get.description: The running job's diff, as `GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}/diff` gives it, as plain text.

parameters.name: X-Diff-Reviewer-Job
parameters.description: The job the agent's prompt named (`--job`). Without it, the request is about the pull request's only queued or running job, and with two it is a `409`: an older run must not take over a newer review.

post.description: The job must be `running` and `headSha` must be its head (`409` otherwise). The review must be one GitHub would take (`400`, saying what to fix): at most 200 inline comments, a summary unless it approves, and every comment's lines in one hunk of the diff's new side. `prType` must be one of the rubric's pull request types, or null when it names none, and each comment's `category` one of that type's categories (see `InlineComment`) (`400`). Comments without an `id` are given one. The job becomes a `draft`, recording `prType` and the rubric's version (0 for none), and the review is the first of its revisions. For a repository in `direct` mode the platform then posts it — always as a comment, whatever its decision, which the job keeps; if posting fails the job is left `approved` with the reason in `error`, and the submission still stands; when the post's outcome was unknown and it is found not to have reached GitHub, the workers post it again, if the pull request is still open at the job's head, up to 3 posts in all.

prType.description: The name of the pull request type reviewed, one of `prTypes`; null when there are none.

status.description: `draft`, or `posted` (or `approved`, if posting failed) in `direct` mode.

post.summary: Settle a post whose outcome is unknown, without posting
post.description: For a job whose `postStartedAt` is set — a post that may have reached GitHub. The pull request's reviews by the operator are searched for the job's marker. Found, the job is `posted`, with GitHub's record in `postedReview`. Not found and the claim older than its window (three times the post's timeout), the claim is cleared and the job left `approved`, free to be moved back to `draft`, rejected, posted again or made `stale`. Not found within the window, a `409`: the post may still be under way. Reviews that cannot be read leave the claim as it is: a `502` that carries the job. `409` too for a job that is not `approved`, not at `version`, or has no claim. The workers do the same on every pass for every claim past its window, so a claim is settled without this too. In a `direct` repository the workers then post a review of their own that did not reach GitHub again, as a comment, if its pull request is still open at the job's head (otherwise the job is made `stale`), up to 3 posts by the platform; past that it is left `approved` with the reason in `error`. A post a person started is never posted again by the workers. A `calibration` job has no post to settle: `409`.

200.description: The job: `posted`, or `approved` without its claim.

502.description: GitHub's reviews could not be read; the claim stands.

get.summary: The history of a job's review
get.description: Every write of the job's review, oldest first: the agent's submission, each person's edit, and what GitHub holds once it is posted. What the agent drafted beside what was posted. Paged: `limit` (default 50, at most 200) and `offset`; `400` for a `limit` or `offset` that is not one. The history is bounded: the agent's first draft, every `github` revision (what was posted) and the last 100 revisions are kept, and older edits between them are dropped.

nextOffset.description: The `offset` of the next page; null on the last.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items in the page.

get.description: The current version; version 0 with an empty document when there is none yet. `404` for a repository that is not registered.

put.description: The body is the whole document with the version it replaces, as last read (`409` if that is no longer the current one). It becomes the next version, and the one it replaces stays in the history. A type's `description`, `rubric` and `categories` default to empty. `400` for a type or category without a name or with the name of another, past 50 types or 50 categories a type, or a rubric past 65536 bytes. The answer of a `GET` may be sent back as it is, edited: its `owner`, `name`, `createdAt` and `documentError` are not kept as the document's, and fields this build does not know, on the document, a type or a category, are kept. A field may be left out (it is then empty) but not `null` (`400`). `409` too while the current version cannot be read by this build (`documentError`): it is left for a build that can.

version.description: The version last read; 0 when the repository had none.

get.summary: Every version of a repository's rubric document
get.description: Newest first. A job's `rubricVersion` names one of them. Paged: `limit` (default 50, at most 200) and `offset`; `400` for a `limit` or `offset` that is not one.

nextOffset.description: The `offset` of the next page; null on the last.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items in the page.

post.summary: Import past reviews by the trusted reviewers
post.description: Queues an import of the most recently updated closed pull requests (`limit`, 50 by default, at most 200); the workers read it on, a bounded number of pull requests a pass, and stop when GitHub says its rate limit is reached, to go on the next pass. Each submitted review by a trusted reviewer becomes a sample, unless one of it is stored already (or was deleted). `409` while an import of the repository is under way (with it, as `import`) or when the repository names no `trustedReviewers`; `503` without a GitHub token.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items in the page.

nextOffset.description: The `offset` of the next page; null on the last.

get.summary: The samples, most recently reviewed first

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items in the page.

nextOffset.description: The `offset` of the next page; null on the last.

delete.description: It is no longer listed or picked for a run, and importing again does not bring it back. The scores of the jobs that reviewed it are kept.

post.description: One `calibration` job per sample, at the sample's commit and with its base for the diff, queued and run as any review is, with the same prompt and rubric, and never posted. `{"samples": [id, …]}` names them; `{"count": n}` takes the n reviewed by the fewest runs so far, the most recent first. At most 20 either way. `429` when the jobs would pass `--max-calibration-jobs-per-day` (20 by default) for the repository, a cap apart from `--max-jobs-per-day`.

get.description: Each with its jobs by status and the aggregate of its scores: the repository's calibration over time.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items in the page.

nextOffset.description: The `offset` of the next page; null on the last.

get.summary: One run, with each sample's result

get.description: Every scored calibration job of the repository by the current matcher, and the same broken down by the rubric version the jobs were reviewed against.

bearerAuth.description: The API token ($DIFF_REVIEWER_API_TOKEN_FILE). The password is not accepted here.

agentBearer.description: The agent token ($DIFF_REVIEWER_AGENT_TOKEN_FILE), which kleis injects into an agent's requests. Reaches `/api/agent/v1/` only.

Error.description: The request was refused; `error` says why.

autoReview.description: Whether the platform lists the repository's open pull requests itself and makes a job for each new head commit (GitHub draft pull requests excepted).

trustedReviewers.description: The GitHub logins, in lower case, whose reviews calibration imports and scores the agent against.

version.description: Incremented by every write of the settings; sent back as `version` to have a stale write refused.

status.description: A `JobStatus`; a status a newer build wrote is shown as it is, and the job is read-only to this one.

queueEntry.description: The orchestra queue entry running the review, once queued: the latest, after following `continuedBy`.

reviewError.description: Why the stored review cannot be read by this build, when it cannot; `review` is then null and the job is read-only.

version.description: Incremented by every write; sent back with the next one.

baseSha.description: The pull request's base commit, from GitHub, once known.

title.description: The pull request's title, from GitHub, once known.

prBody.description: The pull request's description, from GitHub, once known.

error.description: What the platform's last step on the job failed with — queueing, the run, posting — until one succeeds.

prType.description: The pull request type the agent said it reviewed: one of the rubric's types, at `rubricVersion`.

attempts.description: How many times the job has been queued on orchestra.

postStartedAt.description: When posting last began, while its outcome is not known: the claim that keeps the review from being posted twice. While it is set the job cannot leave `approved`, have its review edited or be made `stale` (`409`); posting it again, or `POST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/reconcile`, settles it.

postNote.description: How the review was posted when that differs from its decision: in `direct` mode, or on a pull request the operator wrote, an approval or request for changes is posted as a comment.

postedReview.description: The review as GitHub holds it, once posted: what was posted, which after a post whose outcome was unknown is GitHub's record rather than the job's own review.

rubricVersion.description: The version of the repository's rubric document the review was checked against, recorded with the agent's submission: 0 when the repository had none; null for a job the agent has not reviewed, or one from before rubrics, whose edits are checked against the current rubric.

directPosts.description: How many times the platform has posted the review on its own, in a `direct` repository: the post on submission and each post again after a claim was settled as not having reached GitHub. At most 3; a person's posts are not counted.

postDirect.description: Whether the last post was the platform's own, which it posts again (if the pull request is still open at the job's head, and fewer than 3 times) once its claim is settled as not having reached GitHub. A person's post, edit or move clears it.

kind.description: `review`: a review of a pull request, posted once approved. `calibration`: a review of a past commit, scored against a trusted reviewer's review of it and never approved, edited, claimed or posted. A kind a newer build wrote is shown as it is, and never posted.

sampleId.description: The calibration sample a `calibration` job reviews.

runId.description: The calibration run that asked for a `calibration` job.

comments.description: At most 200. A comment's lines must lie in one hunk of the diff's new side.

Review.description: A `comment` or `request_changes` review must have a non-empty `body`; GitHub refuses either without one. Fields this build does not know, on the review or on a comment, are kept as they are.

suggestion.description: Replacement text for the lines, posted as a GitHub suggestion.

id.description: Stable within the review, and unique in it. A comment written without one is given one by the platform when the review is submitted or edited; one it has is kept. A review stored before ids existed gets them on its next write, not when it is read.

category.description: What the comment is about: one of the categories of the job's pull request type, or free text when that type lists none. A job of no type (reviewed by hand) may use any category of the rubric, or free text when it names none. On a person's edit only a category that is new or changed is checked.

severity.description: How much the comment matters. A severity this build does not know makes a stored review unreadable (`reviewError`), as an unknown decision does.

InlineComment.description: Fields this build does not know are kept as they are and written back on every round trip.

headSha.description: The commit to review, and the one a submission must name.

instructions.description: How to review and how to write the review, in markdown, followed by the repository's default rubric when it has one.

prTypes.description: The repository's pull request types, each with its rubric and categories: the agent picks the one that fits, reviews by its rubric and files its comments under its categories. Empty when the rubric names none.

examples.description: Past reviews to calibrate against; empty for now.

rubricVersion.description: The version of the rubric document these come from; 0 when the repository has none.

Category.description: Fields this build does not know are kept as they are and written back, a `PUT` of the document included.

name.description: Unique in the document; what a submission's `prType` names.

description.description: When the type applies: what the agent picks the type by.

rubric.description: How to review a pull request of this type, in markdown, on top of the default rubric. At most 65536 bytes.

categories.description: What a comment of a review of this type is filed under. Names are unique within the type.

PrType.description: Fields this build does not know are kept as they are and written back, a `PUT` of the document included.

RubricDocument.description: One version of a repository's rubric document. Fields this build does not know are kept as they are and written back, a `PUT` of the document included.

version.description: 1 for the first document and one more for each change; 0 for a repository that has none yet.

createdAt.description: When this version was written; null for version 0.

defaultRubric.description: How to review any pull request of the repository, in markdown; given to the agent in its `instructions`. At most 65536 bytes. Null only with `documentError`.

prTypes.description: The kinds of pull request the repository's reviews tell apart. Null only with `documentError`.

documentError.description: Why this build cannot read the stored document, when it cannot. The agent API then refuses the repository's reviews (`409`) rather than review without the rubric.

Revision.description: One write of a job's review.

version.description: The job's version the write made.

author.description: `agent` (the submission), `person` (an edit) or `github` (what GitHub holds once posted: the job's review with GitHub's body, without the marker, and the event it was posted as when known).

review.description: The review as written, as the JSON stored; not reinterpreted by this build.

reviewError.description: Why the stored review is not JSON, when it is not.

HumanComment.description: A trusted reviewer's inline comment, on the new side of the diff at the review's commit.

line.description: The last line of the range, as GitHub's `original_line` placed it on the review's commit.

CalibrationSample.description: One review a trusted reviewer wrote of one commit of a closed pull request.

reviewId.description: GitHub's id of the review; an import never stores one twice.

state.description: GitHub's state of the review, as it gave it: `APPROVED`, `CHANGES_REQUESTED`, `COMMENTED`, `DISMISSED`.

commitId.description: The commit the review was of: the calibration job's head.

baseSha.description: The merge base of the pull request's base and `commitId`: the base its diff had there.

dropped.description: The review's comments that were not kept: on the old side, not placed on a line of `commitId`, and replies in a thread.

CalibrationImport.description: A request to import the samples of a repository's recent closed pull requests, and how far it has got.

limit.description: How many of the most recently updated closed pull requests it reads.

pullsListed.description: The closed pull requests found, once listed.

known.description: Reviews stored before (or deleted), not stored again.

empty.description: Reviews with no body and no comment kept: nothing to compare.

unreachable.description: Reviews of a commit GitHub could not compare with the base.

unreadable.description: Pull requests whose reviews GitHub refused to list.

error.description: Why the last pass stopped short — GitHub's rate limit, an error to retry — or why it failed.

CalibrationScore.description: One calibration job's draft against its sample. Comments are paired one to one, greedily, closest first: on the same file, with ranges that overlap or are at most 3 lines apart. Pairing is by place only.

matcherVersion.description: The version of the matcher that made the score; scores of different versions are not compared.

precision.description: `matched / agentComments`: how many of the agent's comments were on something the person commented on. To four decimals; null when there is nothing to divide by.

recall.description: `matched / humanComments`: how many of the person's comments the agent found. To four decimals; null when there is nothing to divide by.

comments.description: The agent's comments of this kind.

matched.description: Of them, those paired with one of the person's.

comments.description: The agent's comments of this kind.

matched.description: Of them, those paired with one of the person's.

agree.description: Whether they are one decision; null when the state stands for none (`DISMISSED`).

key.description: `<agent comment id>:<GitHub comment id>`: how a later judge's verdict names the pair.

gap.description: Lines between the two ranges; 0 when they overlap.

agent.description: One of the agent's comments, as it drafted it.

items.description: One of the agent's comments, as it drafted it.

CalibrationAggregate.description: Scores by the current matcher added up: counts first, every ratio computed from the sums, so each comment weighs the same.

precision.description: Matched over the agent's comments. To four decimals; null when there is nothing to divide by.

recall.description: Matched over the person's comments. To four decimals; null when there is nothing to divide by.

comments.description: The agent's comments of this kind.

matched.description: Of them, those paired with one of the person's.

comments.description: The agent's comments of this kind.

matched.description: Of them, those paired with one of the person's.

agreement.description: Agreed over compared. To four decimals; null when there is nothing to divide by.

CalibrationRun.description: A set of calibration jobs asked for together. `results` only in the answer for one run.

score.description: Null until the job's draft is scored.

rubricVersion.description: The rubric version the jobs were reviewed against; 0 for none.
